Done. Reflection complete.

What was generalizable from this WRONG answer (508.06 vs gold 504.12, ~0.78% high):

The methodology was right (|trust receipts Nov 1959 − Dec 1959| × FX); the error was the historical FX rate. The Canadian dollar traded at a PREMIUM to USD in the late-1950s/early-1960s, so USD→CAD < 1 (≈0.9531 in Dec 1959). I used a value too close to parity (~0.96), which inflated the answer. Back-solving confirms the receipts difference (~529 USD-millions) was correct.

Saved:
- New skill: officeqa-trust-receipts-fx-historical-cad — covers locating the trust-account receipts line, the two-stage diff×FX method, and a USD-CAD era cheat-sheet (pre-May 1962 CAD premium → rate ~0.95; post-1962 peg → ~1.081; 1970s+ → >1), with the back-solve verification trick.
- Memory: compact USD-CAD historical-rate-direction fact appended to an existing entry (memory was at capacity, so I merged it in).

This fills a real gap — the existing FX skill only documented modern (1990s–2000s) month-end rates and explicitly flagged that historical rates differ, so the pre-1962 CAD-premium convention was previously undocumented.
